title: Tenma, Osaka: where locals actually eat (one stop from Osaka Station)
description: Skip the Dotonbori queues for one night. Tenma and Japan's longest shopping street, Tenjinbashisuji, are where Osaka eats and drinks: counter sushi from about ¥100 a plate, standing bars after six and a half-day walking route. Plus the ordering trick that gets you seated and eating in minutes. #osaka #osakafood #japantravel
alt_text: Tenjinbashisuji covered shopping arcade in Osaka with a large paper lantern reading Ten-san and local shoppers. Text: Where Osaka locals actually eat

title: Osaka local markets beyond Kuromon: Kizu, Tsuruhashi and Tenjinbashisuji
description: Kuromon is great but busy. These are the markets where Osaka actually shops for dinner, with the station, opening hours and closing day for each, so you don't arrive to shutters. Plus a 1907 sushi counter hidden inside the wholesale market. #osakamarket #osakafood #japantrip
alt_text: Stalls in a covered Osaka food market. Text: Osaka markets beyond Kuromon

title: Where to stay in Tokyo for a first trip: Shinjuku, Tokyo Station or Asakusa/Ueno
description: Three bases, same-night Booking.com prices for two, train times between them and exactly which trips each one makes easy. Pick by what you'll do, not by the hotel photos. #tokyo #wheretostay #tokyotravel #japantravel
alt_text: Red-brick Tokyo Station building with modern towers behind. Text: First time in Tokyo? Pick the right base

title: Your hotel says Shinjuku. Which station will you actually use?
description: Three hotels can all say Shinjuku and sit by three different stations. On the same December night we found doubles from about ¥13,000 near Higashi-shinjuku, ¥15,000 near Shinjuku-sanchome and over ¥22,000 right by JR Shinjuku. Sanchome's subway lines reach Shibuya, Ikebukuro and Ginza with no change. Plus a basement café by the East Exit, serving commuters since 1970, that opens at 7:00. Worth a look before you book. #shinjuku #tokyohotel #tokyotravel #japantravel
alt_text: Colourful Shinjuku station sign in Tokyo. Text: "Shinjuku" hotel? Which station is it really?

title: Narita or Haneda to your Tokyo hotel: which train is fastest?
description: Keikyu or the Monorail from Haneda, Narita Express or Skyliner from Narita, and when the Limousine Bus or a taxi wins. Official times and fares, matched to where your hotel is, so you skip the extra transfer with luggage. #narita #haneda #tokyotravel
alt_text: Narita Express train sign showing arrival at Tokyo Station. Text: Narita or Haneda: which train to your hotel?

title: Kansai Airport to Osaka: Nankai or JR? Pick the train for your hotel
description: Nankai goes to Namba; JR goes to Tennoji, Osaka Station and Shin-Osaka, so choose by where you sleep. Rapi:t reaches Namba in 34–39 min, and the Airport Express takes 43 min for about ¥970 with no reservation. Flying out late? Rinku Town, one stop before the airport, has a free bay park where you watch planes take off at sunset. Times for each hotel area are on the page. #kansaiairport #osaka #japantrains #japantravel
alt_text: Limited express train at a platform on the way from Kansai Airport. Text: Kansai Airport to Osaka: Nankai or JR?

title: Where to stay in Osaka: Namba, Umeda or Tennoji?
description: All three sit on the same red Midosuji line, but what's outside your door is very different. Nightlife and street food, transport hub and shopping, or quieter and cheaper. Here's who each area suits. #osaka #wheretostay #osakahotel
alt_text: Osaka Station entrance sign lit up at night. Text: Where to stay in Osaka: Namba, Umeda or Tennoji?

title: Cloudy forecast for Mount Fuji? What to do with your Kawaguchiko day
description: Grey forecast for Fuji? Check Yamanashi's live Fujisan Watcher cameras the evening before; an unused JR ticket can be changed once for free. No spare day? The Itchiku Kubota Art Museum (¥1,500) and a bowl of Fudo hoto (¥1,210) still make the day. Already booked a night? Keep it: the ¥2,000 two-day bus pass turns one chance at Fuji into two. The cloud-day plan is on the page. #mountfuji #kawaguchiko #fujitrip #japantravel
alt_text: Mount Fuji half hidden by heavy clouds above Lake Kawaguchi. Text: Cloudy Fuji forecast? Don't waste the day

title: Senso-ji without the crowds: before breakfast or after dinner?
description: Senso-ji's grounds never close. Go at 6:30 (Oct–Mar) to step inside the main hall before the crowds, then have a ¥850 miso-soup breakfast nearby from 8:00. After dinner the gates, pagoda and hall stay lit until about 23:00, and the closed Nakamise stalls show their painted shutters. Our photo route and a rakugo theatre five minutes away are on the page. #sensoji #asakusa #tokyotravel #japantravel
alt_text: Senso-ji temple in Asakusa lit up at night. Text: Senso-ji with fewer people: when to go

title: Yanaka Ginza, old Tokyo: which way to walk (downhill route)
description: Start at JR Nippori and the Yuyake Dandan steps come first, going down, into Yanaka Ginza: about 170 m and 60 small shops. Finish at Sendagi, which has a lift to the platform. Walk it the other way and the same steps are the last thing you climb, bags in hand. A step-free route from Sendagi is on the page too. Easy old-Tokyo outing with parents. #yanaka #yanakaginza #oldtokyo #tokyotravel
alt_text: The Yanaka Ginza shopping street gate in Tokyo on a sunny day. Text: Old Tokyo: walk Yanaka Ginza the easy way

title: Minoh Falls in autumn: a half-day from Osaka, back before dark
description: Yes, an autumn afternoon is enough on a weekday: Osaka-umeda 13:00, Minoh 13:26, about 45 minutes up a riverside path to the 33 m falls, back at the station around 15:30, before the 16:48 sunset. Short on time? Turn at Ryuan-ji's red bridge with a bag of momiji tempura (fried maple leaves). Weekend timings and a brewery taproom one stop from Minoh are on the page. #minoh #osakadaytrip #autumninjapan #japantravel
alt_text: Visitors on the viewing terrace in front of Minoh Falls in the forest. Text: Minoh Falls in one autumn afternoon

title: Namba, Osaka beyond the neon: 3 quieter stops a short walk from Dotonbori
description: 1) Namba Yasaka Shrine: a 12 m lion head said to swallow bad luck, free and quiet in the morning, about 8 min on foot. 2) Hozenji Yokocho: a narrow stone alley of old restaurants around a moss-covered temple statue, 3–5 min from Exit 14. 3) Doguyasuji: the kitchen-supply street for knives and plastic food samples, 3 min away. Walking times for every stop are on the page. #namba #osaka #osakatravel #japantravel
alt_text: Dotonbori canal and neon signs in Namba, Osaka on a sunny day. Text: Namba, but quieter: 3 stops a short walk from the canal

title: Where to stay in Osaka if you're out late (the subway stops at midnight)
description: Most Osaka subway lines stop around midnight, so pick your hotel by where you'll be at 1am. Namba puts Dotonbori, the Ura-Namba standing bars and Hozenji Yokocho a short walk away. For a more local night, stay by JR Tenma: the lantern-lit Ura-Tenma izakaya alleys are just north of the station. Plus a 24-hour plan B if you miss the last train. #osakanightlife #osaka #wheretostay #japantravel
alt_text: Dotonbori canal glowing with neon at night. Text: Out late in Osaka? Stay where you can walk home

title: Shibuya Crossing from above: is it worth paying? Free vs ¥1,800 vs Shibuya Sky
description: Free from Hachiko Square, a drink for the Starbucks window (no seat guaranteed), ¥1,800 for the MAG8 rooftop with a drink, or ¥2,700+ for Shibuya Sky. What each view of the scramble really gets you. #shibuya #shibuyacrossing #tokyotravel
alt_text: Shibuya Scramble Crossing seen from above with pedestrians crossing in every direction. Text: Shibuya Crossing: the best view for your budget

title: Hiroshima and Miyajima in one day: 4 stops, and the tide table that decides your afternoon
description: 1) Peace Memorial Museum at 7:30 (book online for the early slot), then the A-Bomb Dome. 2) The JR ferry from Miyajimaguchi: between 9:10 and 16:10 its route passes close to the Great Torii, so stand on the right-hand side. 3) The Great Torii: below about 100 cm of tide you can walk to it, above about 250 cm it floats. 4) Omotesando, where the deer shop too. The guide shows how to pick a day with both tides in daylight, plus where to eat anagomeshi and okonomiyaki. #hiroshima #miyajima #itsukushima #japantravel
alt_text: Four photos: the A-Bomb Dome, a JR ferry on the sea, the red Great Torii standing in the water, a deer at a shop door on Miyajima. Text: Hiroshima + Miyajima in one day; 1 A-Bomb Dome, 2 JR ferry, 3 Great Torii, 4 Omotesando deer

title: Kansai Airport to Kyoto: Haruka, limousine bus or via Osaka? 3 ways in
description: 1) The JR Haruka: about 75 to 80 minutes with no change, ¥2,700 on the visitor one-way ticket. 2) The limousine bus (¥2,800) runs until 23:20, over an hour after the last Haruka at 22:16, and your cases go in the hold. 3) Once you arrive, the Skyway: a free glass corridor 45 metres above Kyoto Station's hall, open 10:00 to 22:00. The guide matches each route to your hotel area and landing time. #kyoto #kansaiairport #japantrains #kyototravel
alt_text: Kyoto Tower against a cloudy sky. Text: Kansai Airport to Kyoto: 3 ways in; ¥2,700 Haruka; Bus until 23:20; Free Skyway 45 m up

title: Osaka Station or Umeda: same place? 3 things to know before you pick a hotel side
description: JR calls it Osaka Station, the private lines and subway call it Umeda: one walkable hub of six stations. 1) Kushikatsu Matsuba Sohonten in the old Shin-Umeda food alley under the tracks: standing-only for about 70 years, skewers in the ¥100s. 2) Ikayaki, the pressed squid pancake, from the Snack Park on B1 of Hanshin Umeda. 3) The Umeda Sky Building's rooftop ring, open until 22:30. The guide shows which side of the station suits the Haruka, the airport bus and families. #osaka #umeda #osakatravel #japantravel
alt_text: The plaza of Osaka Station City seen from above with people crossing. Text: Osaka Station or Umeda? 3 things to know; 70-year kushikatsu bar; Hanshin B1 ikayaki; Sky Building ring

title: Where to stay in Fukuoka on a first trip: Hakata, Tenjin or Nakasu-Kawabata?
description: Hakata for trains (5 minutes from the airport by subway), Tenjin for shopping and Dazaifu, Nakasu-Kawabata for yatai nights. 1) About 100 yatai street stalls, most seating no more than about 10. 2) Yanagibashi Rengo Market, 'Hakata's kitchen': lanes about a metre wide, open from 8:00, closed Sundays. 3) Hakata Ramen Shin-Shin in Tenjin, open since October 2003. The guide adds a simple first afternoon and evening. #fukuoka #hakata #yatai #japantravel
alt_text: A neon-lit street in Fukuoka at night with traffic below. Text: Fukuoka first trip: where to stay; About 100 yatai stalls; Yanagibashi Market; Shin-Shin ramen, 2003

title: New Chitose Airport to Sapporo: train, bus or car? 3 ways in, and where to eat first
description: The JR Rapid Airport train takes 33 to 43 minutes to Sapporo Station for ¥1,230 and you just tap Suica; the ¥1,500 airport bus wins when it stops outside your Odori or Susukino hotel. Before you head down to the trains, eat on the Domestic Terminal's third floor: 1) Baikoken, Asahikawa soy-sauce ramen from a shop founded in 1969. 2) Ebisoba Ichigen, ramen made with sweet-shrimp heads in its red bowls. 3) Ajisai, Hakodate salt ramen with clear soup. The guide also covers what changes on a heavy-snow day. #sapporo #hokkaido #newchitose #japantrains
alt_text: A green-and-white JR Hokkaido train coming through deep snow under overhead wires. Text: New Chitose to Sapporo: 3 ways in; 33 min for ¥1,230; 1969 Asahikawa ramen; Shrimp-head ramen

title: 8 Osaka hotels with real perks: free ramen, rooftop baths and free drinks, by budget
description: For about ¥12,000 a night for two you can get free lounge drinks until 21:00 in Umeda or free breakfast in Shinsaibashi. 1) Dormy Inn Premium Namba: a natural hot-spring bath, then a free bowl of yonaki soba from about 21:30. 2) Candeo Hotels Osaka Namba: a free rooftop SkySpa open 15:00 to 11:00, and tattooed guests are welcome. 3) Candeo Hotels Osaka The Tower: a 31st-floor bath 135 m up that holds a Guinness World Record. The guide shows sample prices and the station each hotel sits by. #osaka #osakahotels #japantravel #wheretostay
alt_text: A Japanese-style hotel twin room with white beds and a patterned lattice window. Text: 8 Osaka hotels with real perks; Free 9:30 pm ramen; Tattoo-OK rooftop bath; Record bath 135 m up

title: Hakone private onsen: in-room bath, private slot or a 2-hour bath room? 3 ways to book
description: Couples who want to bathe together have three options in Hakone, and they are very different evenings. 1) A reservable private bath at a Gora ryokan, filled with milky sulphur water from Owakudani: 50 minutes for two, five groups a day. 2) Hakone Yuryo near Hakone-Yumoto: 19 private open-air bath rooms, 120 minutes, booked online. 3) Irori Saryo Hachiri inside Yuryo, fish and irori-hearth dishes right after your bath. The guide explains which room words really mean hot-spring water. #hakone #onsen #ryokan #japantravel
alt_text: A round wooden Japanese bath tub with a tap and a small wooden stool. Text: Hakone private onsen: 3 ways to book; Milky Owakudani water; 19 private bath rooms; Irori-hearth dinner

title: Where to stay in Kyoto on a first trip: Kyoto Station, Karasuma or Gion?
description: Our pick for most first trips is Shijo-Karasuma: Kyoto Station is 3 minutes by subway, Kawaramachi one Hankyu stop, Arashiyama about 27 minutes. 1) Kyoto Station: JR reaches Fushimi Inari in 6 minutes for ¥150, and Honke Daiichi Asahi has served soy-sauce ramen since 1947 from 6:00. 2) Gion: walk out at dusk into lantern-lit lanes. 3) Breakfast at 7 at Inoda Coffee's main shop, serving its Arabian Pearl blend since 1940 in a machiya. The guide also explains Kyoto's new hotel tax. #kyoto #kyototravel #gion #japantravel
alt_text: Four photos: Kyoto Station's steel atrium, the Kamo River, a Gion street at night and Fushimi Inari's torii tunnel. Text: Kyoto first trip: where to stay; Kyoto Station; Kamo River; Gion at night; Fushimi Inari

title: 3 things to eat in Sapporo: market crab, soup curry and a late miso ramen
description: Where Sapporo eats, beyond Nijo Market. 1) Curb Market, next to Hokkaido's biggest wholesale market: about 60 shops of crab, roe and fish, with restaurants open from 7:00, so you eat what you pick. 2) Soup curry at Garaku, in a basement near Odori: the pork-bone and herb broth simmers for two days and the shop closes when it runs out. 3) Miso ramen to end the night in Susukino, in the 17-shop Ramen Alley or at Keyaki, open until 2 a.m. The guide adds a one-day eating route and where to stay for it. #sapporo #hokkaido #japanesefood #japantravel
alt_text: Red king crabs on ice at a Sapporo market stall with handwritten signs. Text: 3 things to eat in Sapporo; 60-shop Curb Market; 2-day soup curry broth; Ramen until 2 a.m.

title: Kamakura from noon: Great Buddha, Enoden coast, sunset and Hachimangu in one afternoon
description: A noon start from Tokyo still works if you follow Kamakura's closing times. 1) The Great Buddha first: last entry 16:45 in winter, and ¥50 more lets you step inside the statue. 2) The little green Enoden along the coast, ¥200 a ride, to Inamuragasaki. 3) Sunset over Shichirigahama and Enoshima, around 16:30 in winter, just as Hase's temples close. 4) Tsurugaoka Hachimangu after dark: its gates stay open until 20:00. The guide has the minute-by-minute route and where to eat. #kamakura #daytripfromtokyo #enoden #japantravel
alt_text: Four photos: the Great Buddha of Kamakura, an Enoden train by the sea with Enoshima, a sunset on Kamakura beach and the red hall of Tsurugaoka Hachimangu. Text: Kamakura from noon: 4 stops; Great Buddha; Enoden coast; Cape sunset; Hachimangu

title: Where to stay in Naha, Okinawa: Kokusai-dori, Asahibashi or Omoromachi? And do you need a car?
description: Our pick for a first trip is Kokusai-dori: the Yui Rail monorail reaches it from the airport in 13 to 16 minutes, and you don't need a car in Naha. 1) Makishi Public Market, Naha's kitchen since 1950: 75 stalls downstairs with sea grapes and island pork. 2) Upstairs, 12 eateries for soki soba, champuru and rafute. 3) On Sundays about 1.3 km of Kokusai-dori becomes car-free from 12:00 to 18:00. The guide explains when a rental car is worth it for the north. #okinawa #naha #okinawatravel #japantravel
alt_text: Palm-lined main road in central Naha with cars and shops. Text: Where to stay in Naha: 3 bases; Makishi Market, 1950; Soki soba upstairs; Car-free Sundays

title: Gora to Lake Ashi: Hakone Ropeway or the bus? Views one way, shortcut back
description: Most visitors only know the cable car, ropeway and boat loop. 1) The Hakone Ropeway over Owakudani's steam vents: about 30 minutes to Togendai, covered by the Freepass. 2) The sightseeing boat across Lake Ashi to Moto-Hakone, a short walk from Hakone Shrine's lakeside torii. 3) The Tozan bus shortcut: two short rides from Gora to Moto-Hakone in 20 to 30 minutes for ¥910. Our pick is ropeway out, bus back. The guide also has lunch spots like Tamura Ginkatsutei, where tofu katsuni originated. #hakone #lakeashi #hakoneropeway #japantravel
alt_text: Four photos: steam at Owakudani, a sightseeing boat on Lake Ashi, Hakone Shrine's torii at the lake and a Hakone Tozan bus. Text: Gora to Lake Ashi: bus or ropeway?; Owakudani steam; Lake Ashi boat; Shrine torii; Tozan bus

title: 3 Fukuoka dishes, eaten the local way: mizutaki, mentaiko and motsunabe
description: 1) Mizutaki: in Hakata you drink a cup of the plain chicken broth first; Mizutaki Nagano in Tsushimakoji has served it for about 100 years. 2) Mentaiko for breakfast, not as a souvenir: Ganso Hakata Mentaiju opens at 7:00 with a whole roe on rice. 3) Motsunabe ends with champon noodles in the broth, a habit Rakutenchi (Tenjin, 1977) says it started. The guide pairs each dish with a well-known place and a smaller local one, plus a ramen counter that opens at 6 a.m. #Fukuoka #HakataFood #JapanFood #FukuokaTravel
alt_text: Wooden front of a Hakata restaurant with noren curtains in Fukuoka. Text: Fukuoka: 3 dishes eaten the local way. Mizutaki: soup first. Mentaiko breakfast at 7:00. Hotpot ends in champon.

title: Otaru from Sapporo: 4 stops for a half day, 41 minutes by train
description: 1) Sakaimachi street: at Kitaichi Glass Sangokan 167 oil lamps are lit by hand each morning. 2) The former Temiya Line, Hokkaido's first railway (1882): about 1.6 km of old track you can walk through the bank district. 3) The Bank of Japan Otaru Museum, free entry, a warm half hour before the canal lamps come on. The guide has a timed winter half-day route, the market bowl and sushi picks, and when a night in Otaru is worth it. #Otaru #Hokkaido #SapporoTrip #JapanTravel
alt_text: Four photos of Otaru: the snowy canal path with old warehouses, a seafood rice bowl, a rickshaw on a snowy Sakaimachi street, and the old Temiya Line tracks. Text: Otaru: 4 stops from Sapporo. Canal walk, Market seafood bowl, Sakaimachi street, Hokkaido's 1st railway.

title: Shin-Osaka or Osaka Station? Two different stations, and where to stay
description: 1) Every Tokaido and Sanyo Shinkansen stops at Shin-Osaka only; Osaka Station in Umeda has no bullet-train platforms, one JR stop (about 4 minutes) away. 2) Kyoto costs the same ¥580 from both, so a base in Umeda doesn't cost you on day trips. 3) For an early train, remm Shin-Osaka connects directly to the Shinkansen Central gate. The guide covers JR West's 11-minute transfer rule and one hotel pick per type of traveller. #Osaka #Shinkansen #JapanTrains #OsakaTravel
alt_text: White Shinkansen bullet train beside a platform under a steel station roof in Osaka. Text: Shin-Osaka or Osaka Station? Bullet trains: Shin-Osaka only. Same ¥580 to Kyoto. Hotel at the Shinkansen gate.

title: Kyoto Station food halls: gifts beyond yatsuhashi, before your train
description: 1) Sasaya Iori's dorayaki is sold at Daimaru Kyoto only on the 20th to 22nd of each month, around Toji's Kobo-san market. 2) Izuu, the Gion saba-zushi house, has a counter at JR Kyoto Isetan B2: mackerel sushi some say tastes richer half a day later, which suits a train ride. 3) Murakami Juhonten's purple shibazuke at Takashimaya B1, ¥600 for 130 g. The guide pairs five classic gifts with what Kyoto itself buys, across all three stores. #Kyoto #KyotoFood #JapaneseSweets #KyotoTravel
alt_text: Traditional Japanese sweets wrapped in leaves on a shop counter in Kyoto. Text: Kyoto Station: gifts beyond yatsuhashi. Dorayaki 3 days a month. Izuu saba-zushi. Purple shibazuke ¥600.

title: Tokyo Christmas Markets 2026: which are free and which are paid?
description: Tokyo has five Christmas markets this year, all ending 25 December. 1) Roppongi Hills: free entry, its 20th edition, with Käthe Wohlfahrt ornaments and the Keyakizaka lights after 17:00. 2) Skytree Town: no ticket listed, Glühwein in boot-shaped mugs. 3) Tokyo Christmas Market at Shin-Toyosu and Shiba Park: ¥1,000 weekdays, ¥1,500 weekends, and only advance tickets include the mug. The table with dates, hours and nearest exits is on our page. #TokyoChristmas #TokyoTravel #JapanInDecember #ChristmasMarket
alt_text: People walking under trees covered in warm white Christmas lights at night in Tokyo. Text: Tokyo Christmas Markets 2026, Free or paid?

title: Kyoto in December 2026: what's actually on (the lantern path is gone)
description: The Arashiyama Hanatouro lantern path older guides mention ended after 2021. What Kyoto does have in December 2026: 1) radish stew at Senbon Shakado on 7–8 Dec (¥1,000); 2) the year's last flea markets at Toji (21 Dec) and Kitano Tenmangu (25 Dec); 3) on New Year's Eve, temples like Kodaiji where you can ring the bell yourself. The calendar and bell list are on our page. #KyotoTravel #JapanInDecember #Kyoto #JapanTravel
alt_text: A five-storey pagoda in Kyoto with snow on its roofs above old wooden houses. Text: Kyoto in December 2026, What's actually on

title: Sapporo in December 2026: White Illumination and the Christmas Market in one walk
description: Both run 20 Nov–25 Dec 2026 in Odori Park, so one evening covers them. 1) The Munich Christmas Market (25th year): Glühwein, sausages and a yearly mug you keep, cashless at every stall. 2) The Red Brick Office joins the illumination for the first time, lit in blue. 3) Minami 1-jo's 46 ginkgo trees and about 70,000 LEDs on the way to Susukino. Our page has a timed light walk from Sapporo Station. #Sapporo #Hokkaido #JapanInDecember #WinterInJapan
alt_text: Four photos: Sapporo TV Tower above the Odori Park market, the red-brick former Hokkaido Government Office, a snowy tree-lined street, Susukino neon at night. Text: Sapporo in December 2026
